messages.subject: some questions in spatial function
parts:
Hi,

I have run some examples of spatial models in INLA. So far it works fine, even though I am still not familiar with some arguments. Keep learning....

Here are two questions, and I am looking for some answers: 

First, I am pretty interested in the visualization of the spatial function by the use of INLA(). I saw some papers using INLA did generate spatial plots, but I did not find any related function in the manual. I am wondering whether we have to use additional software package to draw maps, especially in using boundary data? 

Second, how to obtain the estimated variance in a whole spatial (or smoothing) function?

Many thanks!!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: some questions in spatial function
parts:
Documentation and tutorials for these things are in development.  It is mostly a matter of bookkeeping in constructing the formulas and to know where to look in the output from inla().

The inla package itself will support direct plotting in simple cases, and you can extract information that can be used by standard plotting R functions as well.

/Finn
